summary: Source decomposition of the cyclotomic-unit route to the Iwasawa main conjecture, read from Rubin's Euler systems monograph draft (Chapters II and III), Greither's 1992 Annales de l'institut Fourier paper, and Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams' notes. Covers: the cyclotomic-unit Euler system for Z_p(1) with its three-case distribution relation and the reason for the extra norm from level mp; the twist to the chi-component and the restriction dictionary; Rubin's finite-level bound II.2.2 with both error lengths retained and the separate proof that they vanish for this twist; Thm. III.2.3's divisibility |A_L^chi| | [E_L^chi : C_{L,chi}] with the two distinct uses of the hypothesis chi(p) not 1; Rubin's Iwasawa theorems II.3.2-II.3.4 with Hyp(K_infinity,T) and Hyp(K_infinity/K); the local-global diagram III.2.6 including the augmentation correction when chi(p) = 1; Thm. III.2.7's divisibility with its explicit J^2 bookkeeping and the Leopoldt-based removal of J; the endpoint Thm. III.2.10 via the four-term class-field-theory sequence; the plus-part formulation and its separation from the Vandiver isomorphism; and Greither's abelian/all-p Thms. 3.1, 3.2, A, B, C with their one-half normalisation and the genuinely necessary cyclicity hypothesis on Delta_2. The upgrades from divisibility to equality (Cors. III.2.4 and III.2.8) and the local-unit index (Thm. III.2.9) are cited by the sources rather than proved there, and are recorded as gaps; the proofs of Rubin Chapters IV, V, VII and of Greither Sec. 3-4 are NOT read.

nodes.title: The cyclotomic-unit Euler system for Z_p(1)
nodes.statement: Take K = Q. Kummer theory identifies H^1(F,Z_p(1)) with the p-adic completion (F^x)^hat for every extension F of Q. Fix a compatible system {zeta_m} of primitive m-th roots of unity with zeta_{mn}^n = zeta_m. Define c-tilde_{m,infinity} = N_{Q(mu_{mp})/Q(mu_m)}(zeta_{mp} - 1), an element of Q(mu_m)^x inside H^1(Q(mu_m),Z_p(1)), and c-tilde_m = N_{Q(mu_m)/Q(mu_m)^+}(c-tilde_{m,infinity}). Then {c-tilde_{m,infinity}, c-tilde_m} is an Euler system for (Z_p(1), Q^ab, p): the required norm relation is the classical distribution relation N_{Q(mu_{m ell})/Q(mu_m)}(zeta_{m ell} - 1) = (zeta_m - 1) if ell divides m, = (zeta_m - 1)^{1 - Fr_ell^{-1}} if ell does not divide m and m > 1, and = (-1)^{ell-1} ell if m = 1; and the Euler polynomial is det(1 - Fr_ell^{-1} x | Z_p(1)^*) = det(1 - Fr_ell^{-1} x | Z_p) = 1 - x for every prime ell not equal to p.
hypotheses: the compatible system {zeta_m} must satisfy zeta_{mn}^n = zeta_m (Rubin fixes such a collection before (2)); with a non-compatible choice the norm in (2) lands on a Galois conjugate of zeta_m - 1, so the norm compatibilities fail as written (packet-authored remark)
the m = 1 case of the distribution relation is genuinely different (it produces (-1)^{ell-1} ell, not a unit), so that conductor must be treated separately

the extra norm N_{Q(mu_{mp})/Q(mu_m)} in the definition of c-tilde_{m,infinity} is imposed precisely so that the collection satisfies N_{Q(mu_{mp})/Q(mu_m)} c-tilde_{mp} = c-tilde_m, i.e. so that it is an Euler system in Rubin's sense; Rubin records that this LOSES information

these are genuine global units or p-units of Q(mu_m) and of its real subfield: zeta_{mp} - 1 is not a root of unity, in contrast with the ratio (zeta^{-1} - 1)/(zeta - 1) = -zeta^{-1}, which is torsion and carries no arithmetic
proofSteps: Kummer theory gives H^1(F,Z_p(1)) = lim_n F^x/(F^x)^{p^n} = (F^x)^hat, so cyclotomic units define Galois cohomology classes.
The classical norm relation for 1 - zeta_m (Rubin's (2), quoted from Lang's Cyclotomic Fields Thm. 6.3.1) supplies the three-case distribution formula.

Because the Euler-system axiom requires compatibility also in the p-direction, one replaces zeta_m - 1 by its norm from level mp; Rubin's Remark 2.1 notes that if p divides m then c-tilde_{m,infinity} = zeta_m - 1, while if p does not divide m the extra norm is a genuine modification.
The Euler polynomial of Z_p(1)^* = Z_p is 1 - x, so the Euler-system relation reduces exactly to the distribution relation.
acceptance: Check that the system is nontorsion: the ratio (zeta_m^{-1} - 1)/(zeta_m - 1) equals -zeta_m^{-1} and is a root of unity, so it is NOT the system used here; the system used is built from zeta_{mp} - 1 and its norms.
Check the m = 1 exceptional value (-1)^{ell-1} ell against the convention for the conductor-1 term of the system.
Check that the Euler polynomial is computed for the DUAL representation Z_p(1)^*, matching Rubin's convention that Euler systems for T are indexed by det(1 - Fr_ell^{-1} x | T^*).

The distribution relation (2) shows that the collection {c-tilde_{m infinity}, c-tilde_m} is an Euler system for (Zp(1), Qab, p) ... since for every prime ell not p, det(1 - Fr_ell^{-1} x | Zp(1)^*) = det(1 - Fr_ell^{-1} x | Zp) = 1 - x.

But if p does not divide m, our definition takes into account that our Euler system must satisfy N_{Q(mu_{mp})/Q(mu_m)} c-tilde_{mp} = c-tilde_m. This causes us to lose some information, and leads to the unwanted hypothesis chi(p) not= 1 in Theorem 2.3 below.

nodes.title: Twisting to the chi-component and the unit-to-cohomology dictionary
nodes.statement: Fix a character chi : G_Q -> O^x of finite order prime to p, assumed EVEN and NONTRIVIAL, with conductor f and fixed field L; put Delta = Gal(L/Q), Q_n the degree-p^n subextension of Q_infinity inside Q(mu_{p^{n+1}}), and L_n = L Q_n. Let T = O_chi, so T^* = Z_p(1) tensor chi^{-1}. Since [L:Q] is prime to p, L intersect Q_n = Q and Delta = Gal(L_n/Q_n) for all n, and restriction gives an isomorphism H^1(Q_n,T^*) = H^1(L_n,T^*)^Delta = (L_n^x tensor-hat O_{chi^{-1}})^Delta = (L_n^x)^chi inside L_n^x tensor-hat O. Twisting the Euler system c-tilde by chi^{-1} (Rubin Prop. II.4.2) gives an Euler system c = c-tilde^{chi^{-1}} for (T^*, Q^ab, p f), whose class c_Q corresponds under the above isomorphism to the product over delta in Gal(Q(mu_f)^+/Q) of (delta c-tilde_f)^{chi^{-1}(delta)}, equivalently the product over delta in Gal(Q(mu_{fp})/Q) of (zeta_{fp}^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)}. The chi-cyclotomic units C_{n,chi} are the O[Gal(L_n/Q)]-submodule of E_n^chi generated by xi_{n,chi} (Def. 2.2: for n = 0 the product over Gal(Q(mu_f)/Q) of (zeta_f^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)}, for n > 0 the product over Gal(Q_n(mu_{f p^{n+1}})/Q_n) of (zeta_{f p^{n+1}}^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)}); at n = 0 this generator is NOT the displayed image of c_Q, which by (6) equals xi_{L,chi}^{1 - chi^{-1}(p)}.
hypotheses: chi is even, nontrivial, of finite order PRIME TO p; the prime-to-p order is what makes the chi-component a direct summand and makes L intersect Q_n = Q

chi is viewed as a Dirichlet character modulo f, with the convention chi(q) = 0 when q divides f and chi(q) = chi(Fr_q) otherwise; this convention matters in the formula c_Q = xi_{L,chi}^{1 - chi^{-1}(p)}
the identification of H^1(Q_n,T^*) with (L_n^x)^chi is by restriction followed by the completed tensor product; it identifies the FULL H^1, not a Selmer subgroup

the definition of xi_{n,chi} differs between n = 0 (product over Gal(Q(mu_f)/Q) of (zeta_f^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)}) and n > 0 (product over Gal(Q_n(mu_{f p^{n+1}})/Q_n) of (zeta_{f p^{n+1}}^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)})
proofSteps: Rubin's Prop. II.4.2 twists an Euler system for Z_p(1) into one for T^* = Z_p(1) tensor chi^{-1}, enlarging the conductor set from p to pf.
Rubin's Lemma II.4.3 computes the image of the twisted class c_Q in L^x tensor-hat O under the restriction dictionary, yielding the displayed product over Gal(Q(mu_f)^+/Q).
Definition 2.2 packages the resulting elements as the groups C_{n,chi} of chi-cyclotomic units inside E_n^chi.
acceptance: Check that the twisted system lives over the enlarged conductor set pf and that its Euler factors are the chi-twists of 1 - x.
Check the two-case definition of xi_{n,chi}: at n = 0 the root of unity has conductor f, at n > 0 it has conductor f p^{n+1}.
Check the convention chi(p) = 0 when p divides f, which makes 1 - chi^{-1}(p) a unit whenever chi(p) is not 1.

sources.excerpt: Let T = O_chi as in Sec. 1, so that T^* = Zp(1) tensor chi^{-1}. The restriction map gives an isomorphism (using (1)) H^1(Qn, T^*) = H^1(Ln, T^*)^Delta = (Ln^x tensor-hat O_{chi^{-1}})^Delta = (Ln^x)^chi contained in Ln^x tensor-hat O
sources.match: Gives the restriction dictionary between Galois cohomology and chi-components of units, as recorded in the statement.

sources.excerpt: The Euler system c-tilde for Zp(1) constructed in Sec. 2.1 gives rise (by Proposition II.4.2) to an Euler system c = c-tilde^{chi^{-1}} for (T^*, Qab, pf). By Lemma II.4.3, the image of cQ in L^x tensor-hat O under (3) is prod_{delta in Gal(Q(mu_f)+/Q)} (delta c-tilde_f)^{chi^{-1}(delta)} = prod_{delta in Gal(Q(mu_{fp})/Q)} (zeta_{fp}^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)}.

sources.excerpt: If n >= 0 we let En denote the group of global units of Ln. We define the group of chi-cyclotomic units C_{n,chi} to be the subgroup of En^chi generated over O[Gal(Ln/Q)] by xi_{n,chi} = prod_{delta in Gal(Q(mu_f)/Q)} (zeta_f^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)} if n = 0, prod_{delta in Gal(Qn(mu_{f p^{n+1}})/Qn)} (zeta_{f p^{n+1}}^delta - 1)^{chi^{-1}(delta)} if n > 0.
sources.match: Gives the two-case definition of the chi-cyclotomic units recorded in the hypotheses.

nodes.title: Rubin's finite-level bound II.2.2 with its two error lengths
nodes.statement: Suppose p > 2 and T satisfies Hyp(K,T): (i) there is tau in G_K acting trivially on mu_{p^infinity}, on (O_K^x)^{1/p^infinity} and on K(1), with T/(tau-1)T free of rank one over O; and (ii) T tensor k is an irreducible k[G_K]-module. (These are Rubin's Hyp(K,T). The conditions dim_Phi(V/(tau-1)V) = 1 and V irreducible over Phi[G_K] form the weaker Hyp(K,V), which Rubin uses only for the finiteness Thm. II.2.3.) If c is an Euler system for T then length_O(S_{Sigma_p}(K,W^*)) <= ind_O(c) + n_W + n^*_W, where ind_O(c) = sup{n : c_K in p^n H^1(K,T) + H^1(K,T)_tors} (possibly infinite), n_W = length_O(H^1(Omega/K,W) intersect S^{Sigma_p}(K,W)), n^*_W = length_O(H^1(Omega/K,W^*) intersect S_{Sigma_p}(K,W^*)), and Omega = K(1)K(W)K(mu_{p^infinity},(O_K^x)^{1/p^infinity}). The bound is for the RESTRICTED Selmer group S_{Sigma_p}, with no condition imposed at p; the true Selmer group is reached only through global duality (Thm. II.2.10).
hypotheses: p > 2 is required for Thm. II.2.2; Rubin notes separately that Thm. 2.3 (finiteness) holds even if p = 2 and that Thm. II.3.3 also applies when p = 2
Hyp(K,T)(i) is used to guarantee a supply of primes q with H^1_f(K(q),W_M) and H^1_s(K(q),W_M^*) free of rank one over O/MO -- Rubin states this in Remark 2.6
if rank_O(T) = 1 then Hyp(K,T)(i) holds with tau = 1 and (ii) holds as well (Remark 2.4); this is why the cyclotomic application needs no large-image hypothesis
the two error lengths n_W and n^*_W are part of the statement and are NOT in general zero; Rubin's Remark 2.5 says only that they are frequently zero
ind_O(c) = infinity when c_K is torsion, in which case the bound is vacuous (Remark 2.8)
proofSteps: Rubin proves Thm. II.2.2 in Chapter V Sec. 2 from the derived classes constructed in Chapter IV; that proof was NOT read for this packet.

Remark 2.9 makes explicit that the object bounded is S_{Sigma_p}(K,W^*), because no local condition at p has been imposed on T or on c, so 'that restricted Selmer group is all that the Euler system can see'.

Thm. II.2.10(ii), under its standing hypothesis that loc^s_{Sigma_p}(c_K) is nonzero, upgrades the bound to the true Selmer group: length_O(S(K,W^*)) <= length_O(H^1_s(K_p,T)/O loc^s_{Sigma_p}(c_K)) + n_W + n^*_W, by combining Thm. II.2.2 with Corollary I.7.5 (global duality) applied to the index [S(K,W^*) : S_{Sigma_p}(K,W^*)] = [H^1_s(K_p,T) : O loc^s_{Sigma_p}(S^{Sigma_p}(K,T))].
acceptance: Check that the two error terms are retained downstream unless separately proved to vanish; Rubin's own cyclotomic application does prove their vanishing.
Check the distinction between S_{Sigma_p} and S: the Euler system alone bounds only the former, and the passage to the latter costs the local index at p.
Check that the conclusion is a length bound, which becomes a divisibility of orders only after the module is known to be finite.

nodes.title: Verification of Hyp(Q,T^*) and vanishing of n_W, n^*_W for the cyclotomic twist
nodes.statement: For T^* = Z_p(1) tensor chi^{-1} with chi even, nontrivial, of finite prime-to-p order, one has rank_O T^* = 1, so Hyp(Q,T^*) holds with tau = 1 by Rubin's Remark II.2.4. In this situation Omega = L(mu_{p^infinity}), and Rubin's Lemma III.1.1 shows that both error terms n_{W^*} and n^*_{W^*} of Theorem II.2.2 are ZERO. The vanishing criterion is: if rho is a character not congruent to 1 modulo p then k_rho^Delta = 0 and hence H^1(Omega/K, D_rho) = 0; it is applied with rho = chi and with rho = chi^{-1} epsilon_cyc. Rubin's Lemma III.1.1 has two parts: (i) if chi is not 1 then H^1(L(mu_{p^infinity})/K, W) = 0; (ii) if chi is not congruent to the cyclotomic character modulo the maximal ideal of O then H^1(L(mu_{p^infinity})/K, W^*) = 0. The proof of Thm. III.2.3 invokes it 'since chi is nontrivial and even'.
hypotheses: chi has order prime to p, so chi is not congruent to 1 modulo p unless chi is trivial: nontriviality gives Lemma 1.1(i) (rho = chi). Lemma 1.1(ii) (rho = chi^{-1} epsilon_cyc) needs chi not congruent to epsilon_cyc modulo the maximal ideal; for p > 2 evenness supplies this, since complex conjugation acts by 1 through chi and by -1 through epsilon_cyc (this reduction is review-authored; Rubin only cites 'nontrivial and even')
the criterion is applied to both the module and its Tate dual (rho = chi and rho = chi^{-1} epsilon_cyc)
rank_O T^* = 1 gives Hyp(Q,T^*) with tau = 1; no large-image assumption is available or needed here
proofSteps: Rubin's Lemma III.1.1 proves H^1(Omega/K, k_rho) = 0 implies H^1(Omega/K, D_rho)_p = 0 implies H^1(Omega/K, D_rho) = 0, and identifies k_rho^Delta = 0 when rho is not congruent to 1 mod p.
Applying the criterion with rho = chi gives part (i) and with rho = chi^{-1} epsilon_cyc gives part (ii); these are exactly the two modules W and W^* appearing in n_W and n^*_W.
Rubin records the conclusion in the proof of Thm. III.2.3.
acceptance: Check that this vanishing is proved for THIS twist and is not general; Rubin's Remark II.2.5 gives only finiteness in general.
Check that when p divides the order of chi the setup changes: Remark 2.5 says Thm. II.2.2 still applies but the Selmer group is no longer exactly the ideal class group.
Check the identification Omega = L(mu_{p^infinity}) against the general definition with K = Q.

T = O(1)). Frequently the 'error terms' n_W and n^*_W in Theorem 2.2 are zero; see the examples in Chapter III.

nodes.title: The finite-level divisibility |A_L^chi| divides [E_L^chi : C_{L,chi}]
nodes.statement: Suppose p > 2 and chi(p) is not 1. Then |A_L^chi| divides [E_L^chi : C_{L,chi}], where A_L is the p-part of the ideal class group of L, E_L the global units and C_{L,chi} the chi-cyclotomic units. The proof identifies c_Q = xi_{L,chi}^{1-chi^{-1}(p)} (with chi(p) = 0 when p divides f), observes that 1 - chi^{-1}(p) is a unit of O because chi(p) is not 1 and chi has prime-to-p order, so c_Q generates C_{L,chi}; computes ind_O(c) = length_O(E_L^chi/C_{L,chi}) using that L^x/E_L is torsion-free and that E_L^chi is free of rank one over O by the Dirichlet unit theorem (using p > 2, chi even, chi nontrivial); and identifies S_{Sigma_p}(Q,W) with S(Q,W) = Hom_O(A_L^chi,D) because H^1_ur(Q_p,V) = V^I/(Fr_p - 1)V^I = V^I/(chi(p)-1)V^I = 0 when chi(p) is not 1.
hypotheses: p > 2 and chi(p) not equal to 1; the second hypothesis is, by Rubin's Remark 2.1, an artefact of the Euler-system normalisation and not intrinsic to the theorem
chi even, nontrivial, of prime-to-p order; evenness and nontriviality are used in the Dirichlet-unit-theorem step to get rank exactly one
chi(p) = 0 by convention when p divides f, in which case 1 - chi^{-1}(p) = 1

the identification S(Q,W) = Hom_O(A_L^chi,D) is Rubin's Prop. I.6.1 and is valid because chi has order prime to p; Remark 2.5 warns that when p divides the order of chi the Selmer group is no longer exactly the ideal class group
proofSteps: Apply Thm. II.2.2 to the twisted Euler system c; the error terms vanish by the sibling lemma.
Compute c_Q: by (2) and (4), c_Q = xi_{L,chi}^{1 - chi^{-1}(p)} in H^1(Q,T^*), so under the hypothesis chi(p) not 1 the exponent is a unit and c_Q generates C_{L,chi}.

Compute ind_O(c): since L^x/E_L is torsion-free, ind_O(c) is the largest power of p dividing a generator of C_{L,chi} inside E_L^chi; since E_L^chi is free of rank one over O, ind_O(c) = length_O(E_L^chi/C_{L,chi}).
Identify the Selmer group: by Lemma I.3.2(i), H^1_ur(Q_p,V) = V^I/(Fr_p-1)V^I = V^I/(chi(p)-1)V^I = 0 since chi(p) is not 1, hence H^1_f(Q_p,W) = 0 and S_{Sigma_p}(Q,W) = S(Q,W) = Hom_O(A_L^chi,D).
Combine: |S_{Sigma_p}(Q,W)| divides [E_L^chi : C_{L,chi}], which is the assertion.
acceptance: Check that the hypothesis chi(p) not 1 enters TWICE and for different reasons: to make c_Q a generator of C_{L,chi}, and to kill the local condition at p. A proof removing it must address both.
Check that the Dirichlet unit theorem step gives rank exactly one for E_L^chi: this uses p > 2, chi even and chi nontrivial.
Check the torsion-freeness of L^x/E_L, which converts the index of divisibility into a module length.
Check that this is a divisibility of orders and that the upgrade to equality is a separate analytic input.

nodes.title: Rubin's Iwasawa-theoretic Euler-system theorems II.3.2-II.3.4
nodes.statement: Fix an abelian extension K_infinity/K with Gal(K_infinity/K) isomorphic to Z_p^d and such that NO FINITE PRIME OF K SPLITS COMPLETELY IN K_infinity. Let c be an Euler system for (T, K_infinity) in Rubin's sense (an Euler system for (T, K-script, N) whose field K-script contains K_infinity), Lambda = O[[Gamma]], S_{Sigma_p}(K_infinity,W^*) the direct limit of the restricted Selmer groups, X_infinity = Hom_O(S_{Sigma_p}(K_infinity,W^*),D), H^1_infinity(K,T) the inverse limit of H^1(F,T) along corestriction, and ind_Lambda(c) = {phi(c_{K,infinity}) : phi in Hom_Lambda(H^1_infinity(K,T),Lambda)}. Then: (II.3.2) if c_{K,infinity} is not in the Lambda-torsion submodule of H^1_infinity(K,T) and V satisfies Hyp(K_infinity,V), then X_infinity is a torsion Lambda-module (the weak Leopoldt conjecture for T); (II.3.3) if T satisfies Hyp(K_infinity,T) and Hyp(K_infinity/K), then char(X_infinity) divides ind_Lambda(c); (II.3.4) if only V satisfies Hyp(K_infinity,V) together with Hyp(K_infinity/K), there is a nonnegative integer t with char(X_infinity) dividing p^t ind_Lambda(c). Moreover (Prop. II.3.7) there is an exact sequence 0 -> H^1_{infinity,s}(K_p,T)/loc^s_{Sigma_p}(H^1_infinity(K,T)) -> Hom_O(S(K_infinity,W^*),D) -> X_infinity -> 0.
hypotheses: the no-completely-split-finite-prime hypothesis on K_infinity/K is part of the setup of Rubin's Sec. II.3 and is not removable there

Hyp(K_infinity,T)(i) requires tau in G_{K_infinity} acting trivially on mu_{p^infinity}, on (O_K^x)^{1/p^infinity} and on K(1), with T/(tau-1)T FREE OF RANK ONE OVER O; (ii) requires T tensor k irreducible as a k[G_{K_infinity}]-module -- over G_{K_infinity}, not over G_K

Hyp(K_infinity/K) is a separate weak assumption: if rank_{Z_p}(Gamma) = 1 and G_{K_infinity} acts trivially or by the cyclotomic character on V, then either K is totally real with Leopoldt known for K, or K is imaginary quadratic; it holds when K = Q
Thm. II.3.3 gives an INTEGRAL divisibility, Thm. II.3.4 only a divisibility up to an unspecified power p^t; the weakening is the price of assuming only Hyp(K_infinity,V)
for Prop. II.3.7 one must assume the corestriction and restriction compatibilities of the H^1_f at the layers, which Rubin states explicitly
proofSteps: Rubin describes the method: 'Essentially by proving analogues of Theorem 2.2 for each field F, K subset F subset K_infinity, we can pass to the limit and prove an Iwasawa-theoretic version of Theorem 2.2.' The proofs are in Chapter VII and were NOT read for this packet.
Prop. 3.7 is proved from Corollary B.3.4, which identifies H^1_infinity(K,T) with the inverse limit of the restricted Selmer modules S^{Sigma_p}(F,T).
Rubin records the implications Hyp(K_infinity,T) => Hyp(K_infinity,V) => Hyp(K,V) and Hyp(K_infinity,T) => Hyp(K,T).

nodes.title: The local-global comparison diagram for cyclotomic units (Rubin Prop. III.2.6)
nodes.statement: With Lambda = O[[Gal(Q_infinity/Q)]], A_infinity = lim A_n, E_infinity = lim (E_n)^hat, C_{infinity,chi} = lim (C_{n,chi})^hat, U_infinity = lim (U_n)^hat the semilocal units, Y_infinity = lim (L_{n,p}^x)^hat, and E'_infinity the inverse limit of the p-units: (i) there is a commutative diagram of horizontal inclusions and surjections Lambda{c_{Q_n}} -> H^1_infinity(Q,T^*) -> H^1_infinity(Q_p,T^*) onto H^1_{infinity,s}(Q_p,T^*) with vertical isomorphisms onto C_{infinity,chi} -> (E'_infinity)^chi -> Y_infinity^chi onto Y_infinity^chi/U_infinity^chi; (ii) Y_infinity^chi/U_infinity^chi is isomorphic as a Lambda-module to 0 if chi(p) is not 1, and to O if chi(p) = 1; (iii) there is a Lambda-module injection (E'_infinity)^chi/E_infinity^chi into O.
hypotheses: the injectivity of the middle horizontal map in (i) rests on Leopoldt's conjecture, which Rubin notes 'is known in this setting' (abelian fields); it is an input, not a formality

(ii) is precisely the augmentation-type correction appearing when chi is trivial on the decomposition group at p: Y_infinity^chi/U_infinity^chi is isomorphic to Z_p[Delta/Delta_p]^chi, nonzero exactly when chi is trivial on Delta_p, i.e. when chi(p) = 1
(iii) follows from (ii) because E_infinity^chi is the kernel of (E'_infinity)^chi -> Y_infinity^chi/U_infinity^chi; the cokernel is therefore at worst O
the identification of H^1_f(Q_{n,p},T^*) with U_n^chi is the local analogue of the global restriction dictionary
proofSteps: The left-hand vertical isomorphism is Lemma II.4.3 again, showing that the image of c_{Q_n} in (L_n^x)^chi is xi_{n,chi}.
The middle vertical isomorphism uses S^{p}(Q_n,T^*) = (E'_n)^chi (Chapter I Sec. 6.3) together with Corollary B.3.4, which gives lim_n H^1(Q_n,T^*) = lim_n S^{p}(Q_n,T^*).
The local row is the restriction isomorphism H^1(Q_{n,p},T^*) = (L_{n,p}^x)^chi carrying H^1_f(Q_{n,p},T^*) onto U_n^chi.

For (ii) Rubin computes by valuations that L_{m,p}^x/U_m = sum over w|p of Z_w = Z[Delta/Delta_p] compatibly with the norm maps, so Y_infinity^chi/U_infinity^chi = Z_p[Delta/Delta_p]^chi, nonzero exactly when chi is trivial on the decomposition group Delta_p.

nodes.title: char(A_infinity^chi) divides char(E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) (Rubin Thm. III.2.7)
nodes.statement: For chi even, nontrivial, of finite prime-to-p order, char(A_infinity^chi) divides char(E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) as ideals of Lambda = O[[Gal(Q_infinity/Q)]]. Here A_infinity = lim (A_n)^hat is the inverse limit of the p-completed ideal class groups of L_n, which under class field theory is the module the atlas stage text (in RJW's notation) names Y_infinity. Notation warning: in Rubin's own notation Y_infinity = lim (L_{n,p}^x)^hat is the SEMILOCAL multiplicative group of Prop. III.2.6, not a class-group module. NO hypothesis chi(p) not 1 is needed. Rubin remarks after Cor. 2.4 that 'Theorem II.3.3 also applies when p = 2'; he does not state that the other inputs of this proof (Prop. 2.6, [Iw3] Thm. 25, the Leopoldt step) hold verbatim at p = 2, so the case p = 2 of Thm. III.2.7 is not established by the passages read.
hypotheses: Hyp(Q_infinity,T^*) is satisfied with tau = 1 because rank_O T^* = 1; this is the only large-image input and it is automatic in rank one
Hyp(Q_infinity/Q) holds because K = Q

the final step, that char(A_infinity^chi) is not divisible by the augmentation ideal J, uses Leopoldt's conjecture for the real abelian field L via the fact that L has no Z_p^2-extension; Rubin says 'We only sketch the proof' for this step
the input [Iw3] Theorem 25 (Iwasawa), that Y_infinity^chi (Rubin's semilocal Y_infinity = lim (L_{n,p}^x)^hat) is a torsion-free finitely generated rank-one Lambda-module, is an external citation
proofSteps: Apply Thm. II.3.3 together with Prop. II.3.7 to obtain char(Hom_O(S(Q_infinity,W),D)) divides ind_Lambda(c) char(H^1_{infinity,s}(Q_p,T^*)).

By [Iw3] Thm. 25, Y_infinity^chi is torsion-free, finitely generated and of rank one over Lambda; since (E'_infinity)^chi is a nonzero Lambda-submodule it is too. With the diagram of Prop. 2.6(i) this gives ind_Lambda(c) = char((E'_infinity)^chi/C_{infinity,chi}).
By Prop. 2.6(iii), (E'_infinity)^chi/E_infinity^chi injects into O, so ind_Lambda(c) divides J char(E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) with J = char(O) the augmentation ideal.

By the Selmer identification (5), Hom_O(S(Q_infinity,W),D) = A_infinity^chi, and by Prop. 2.6 char(H^1_{infinity,s}(Q_p,T^*)) divides J. Hence char(A_infinity^chi) divides J^2 char(E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}).

It remains to show J does not divide char(A_infinity^chi). A standard Iwasawa argument gives J | char(A_infinity^chi) if and only if A_infinity^chi/J A_infinity^chi is infinite, and identifies A_infinity^chi/J A_infinity^chi with Gal(M_infinity/L_infinity) for M_infinity an extension of L_infinity abelian over L. Since chi is even, L is real abelian, Leopoldt holds for L, so class field theory gives that L has no Z_p^2-extension; hence Gal(M_infinity/L) has Z_p-rank one and [M_infinity : L_infinity] is finite. Rubin gives this last step only as a sketch.
acceptance: Check the J^2 bookkeeping: the divisibility is first proved up to J^2 and only then cleaned up; a statement without the augmentation correction is not what the argument produces.

Check the naming dictionary: Rubin's A_infinity^chi (inverse limit of class groups) corresponds under class field theory to the atlas's Y_infinity^chi, so the atlas's phrasing of Rubin III.2.7 is consistent once that identification is made.

nodes.title: The p-adic L-function and the local-unit index char(U_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) = L_chi Lambda
nodes.statement: Let omega be the Teichmuller character giving the action of G_Q on mu_p (p odd) or mu_4 (p = 2), so omega^{-1} epsilon_cyc is a character of Gal(Q_infinity/Q). Fix an embedding O into Qbar_p and identify complex and p-adic finite-order characters. Then (i) there is an element L_chi in Lambda such that for every k >= 1 and every finite-order character rho of Gal(Q_infinity/Q), (omega^{-1} epsilon_cyc)^k rho (L_chi) = (1 - omega^{-k} rho chi(p) p^{k-1}) L(1-k, omega^{-k} rho chi); and (ii) char(U_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) = L_chi Lambda. Statement (ii) is Iwasawa's theorem identifying the characteristic ideal of the SEMILOCAL unit quotient with the p-adic L-function; it is the chi-component form of the statement the atlas assigns to the Coleman-map owner.
hypotheses: the interpolation in (i) is at the characters (omega^{-1} epsilon_cyc)^k rho for k >= 1, with the Euler factor at p removed in the form (1 - omega^{-k} rho chi(p) p^{k-1})
the identification of complex and p-adic characters requires a fixed embedding O into Qbar_p into C; L_chi depends on that choice
U_infinity is the inverse limit of the SEMILOCAL units U_n of L_{n,p} = L_n tensor Q_p, not the global units; the quotient is by the closure of the cyclotomic units inside them

Rubin does not prove (i) or (ii); he cites [Iw2] Sec. 6 or [Wa] Thm. 7.10 for (i), and [Iw1], [Wa] Thm. 13.56, [Lan] Thm. 7.5.2, or Gillard's Theoreme 1 for the general case of (ii), noting that his Appendix D Sec. 2 carries out the main computation for (ii)

Greither's Cor. 2.14 compares V_rho(U_infinity/C_infinity) with O_p(chi)[[T]]/(G_p(T,rho))^*(1) as Q_p Lambda_rho-modules, i.e. after tensoring with Q_p: it determines the characteristic ideal only up to powers of p, so integrality needs a separate input (for instance mu = 0); the two modules are isomorphic when chi(p) is not 1

For an even chi of arbitrary conductor f Rubin attributes (ii) to Gillard [Gi] Theoreme 1 (not read); the supplier stage ColemanPowerSeries:L4 (RJW Thm. 12.23) states only the tower Q(mu_{p^infinity})^+, i.e. the characters of Gal(Q(mu_p)^+/Q)
proofSteps: Rubin states Thm. 2.9 with references; the proof of (ii) reduces, via the Coleman map, to a computation he says is carried out in Appendix D Sec. 2 (not read for this packet).

Greither's Sec. 2 gives an independent route to the same computation for general abelian fields unramified at p, including p = 2: Thm. 2.4 (Coleman's exact sequence), Thm. 2.6 (the kernel of the Coleman trace operator is R(1-X)), Thm. 2.8 (a four-term exact sequence), and Thm. 2.13 with Cor. 2.14, which compute the characteristic ideal of V_rho(U_infinity/C_infinity) as that of O_p(chi)[[T]]/(G_p(T,rho))^*(1).

Check the comparison between Rubin's chi-component form char(U_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) = L_chi Lambda and the plus-part form U_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ = Z_p[[G^+]]/(I(G^+) zeta_p) owned by the Coleman-map stage of the atlas; the two differ by coefficient ring and by single-component versus whole-even-part packaging.

nodes.title: The main-conjecture endpoint char(Z_infinity^chi) = L_chi Lambda (Rubin Thm. III.2.10)
nodes.statement: Let M_infinity be the maximal abelian p-extension of L_infinity unramified outside primes above p and let Z_infinity = Gal(M_infinity/L_infinity). Then Z_infinity is a Gal(L/Q)-module and a finitely generated Lambda-module, and char(Z_infinity^chi) = L_chi Lambda. The proof: class field theory gives the four-term exact sequence 0 -> E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi} -> U_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi} -> Z_infinity^chi -> A_infinity^chi -> 0; applying Corollary 2.8 (char(A_infinity^chi) = char(E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi})) and Theorem 2.9(ii) (char(U_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) = L_chi Lambda) together with multiplicativity of characteristic ideals in exact sequences gives the result.
hypotheses: the exact sequence is the class-field-theory sequence of de Shalit Sec. III.1.7; it relates GLOBAL units, SEMILOCAL units, the p-ramified Galois group and the class groups, in that order

Rubin states multiplicativity of char for all finitely generated Lambda-modules (with char = 0 for non-torsion modules); cancelling char(E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) = char(A_infinity^chi) from both sides requires this ideal to be nonzero, i.e. A_infinity^chi torsion (classical Iwasawa theory); Rubin's two-line proof leaves this implicit
the statement is for a fixed even nontrivial chi of prime-to-p order; the trivial character and the odd characters are not covered by this argument
proofSteps: Split the four-term sequence into two short exact sequences and apply multiplicativity of characteristic ideals.
Substitute char(A_infinity^chi) = char(E_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) from Cor. 2.8; the two outer terms cancel.
Substitute char(U_infinity^chi/C_{infinity,chi}) = L_chi Lambda from Thm. 2.9(ii) to obtain char(Z_infinity^chi) = L_chi Lambda.

nodes.title: The plus-part formulation and its separation from the Vandiver isomorphism
nodes.statement: In the plus-part formulation of Rodrigues Jacinto-Williams, with F_n = Q(mu_{p^n}) and F_n^+ its maximal real subfield, X_infinity^+ = Gal(M_infinity^+/F_infinity^+) where M_infinity^+ is the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F_infinity^+ unramified outside the prime above p, and Y_infinity^+ = Gal(L_infinity^+/F_infinity^+) with L_infinity^+ the maximal unramified abelian pro-p extension, so that Y_n^+ = Gal(L_n^+/F_n^+) = Cl(F_n^+) tensor Z_p, the Iwasawa Main Conjecture (their Thm. 13.8) states that X_infinity^+ is a finitely generated torsion Lambda(Gamma^+)-module with ch_{Lambda(Gamma^+)}(X_infinity^+) = I(Gamma^+)_{zeta_p}. This is an equality of IDEALS. Their Thm. 13.11 is a strictly stronger MODULE ISOMORPHISM X_infinity^+ = Lambda(Gamma^+)/I(Gamma^+)_{zeta_p}, proved only under the hypothesis that p is a Vandiver prime (p does not divide h_1^+ = #Cl(F_1^+)). The bridge is Cor. 13.14's exact sequence 0 -> E_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ -> U_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ -> X_infinity^+ -> Y_infinity^+ -> 0; under Vandiver, Cor. 13.16 gives Y_infinity^+ = 0 and E_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ = 0, collapsing the sequence to an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Thm. 13.11's hypothesis is that p is a Vandiver prime; this is NOT known for all p
Cor. 13.16 derives Y_infinity^+ = 0 from Vandiver via Prop. 13.15 (the control statement (Y_infinity^+)_{Gamma_n^+} = Y_n^+) and Nakayama's lemma; the derivation is genuinely two-step

Prop. 13.13's exact sequence 0 -> E_{infinity,1}^+ -> U_{infinity,1}^+ -> Gal(M_infinity^+/L_infinity^+) -> 0 comes from global class field theory at each finite level and an inverse limit justified by the Mittag-Leffler condition
Leopoldt's conjecture for F_n = Q(mu_{p^n}) (known here by a theorem of Brumer, as RJW note) is quoted as an input to the rank of E_n
proofSteps: For the nontrivial even characters chi of Gal(Q(mu_p)/Q) (conductor p, order prime to p), the components of the ideal equality are Rubin Thm. III.2.10, char(Z_infinity^chi) = L_chi Lambda, once RJW's I(Gamma^+)_{zeta_p} is matched with Rubin's L_chi (dictionary not established in the passages read). The trivial-character component, where zeta_p has its pole, is not covered by Rubin's theorem (chi is nontrivial throughout Rubin III.2) and needs a separate argument that was not read.
The passage from componentwise statements to the plus-part statement is the standard idempotent decomposition, available because the relevant group has order prime to p when p is odd.

Under Vandiver, Cor. 13.16(i) gives Y_infinity^+ = 0 and (iii) gives E_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ = 0, so Cor. 13.14's sequence becomes U_{infinity,1}^+/C_{infinity,1}^+ = X_infinity^+, and the Coleman-map computation of the left-hand side yields Thm. 13.11.
acceptance: Check that the atlas stage's endpoint is the IDEAL equality, not the module isomorphism; asserting the latter without Vandiver would be an unjustified strengthening.
Check that the plus-part idempotent decomposition is valid only when p is odd; at p = 2 the even/odd splitting over Z_2 is not available, which is the point of the separate p = 2 treatment at L4.
Check that Cor. 13.16(iii) uses the finite-level index [V_n^+ : D_n^+] = h_n^+, i.e. the cyclotomic-unit index formula.

Check the dictionary between RJW's I(Gamma^+)_{zeta_p} and Rubin's L_chi Lambda (Euler factor, Teichmuller twist, trivial component) before identifying Thm. 13.8 with the recombination of Rubin III.2.10.

nodes.title: Greither's even-character divisibility for abelian fields unramified at p (Thm. 3.1)
nodes.statement: Let F/Q be abelian and unramified at p (p arbitrary, INCLUDING p = 2), K_n = F(mu_{p^{n+1}}), K_infinity their union, X = lim A(K_n) with A the p-class group, E_n the pro-p part of the closure of the global units of K_n in the semilocal units, E_infinity = lim E_n, and C_infinity the inverse limit of the circular units. Then for every even character rho not equal to 1 of Delta_0 = Gal(K_0/Q), the characteristic ideal of the Lambda_rho-module X_rho divides the characteristic ideal of (E_infinity/C_infinity)_rho. Greither records that for rho = 1 one can show char(X_rho) = char((E_infinity/C_infinity)_rho) = (1), and that equality in Thm. 3.1 is a byproduct of the proof of Thm. 3.2.
hypotheses: F/Q abelian and UNRAMIFIED AT p; the argument is set up for this class of fields and Greither performs conductor-reduction steps rather than assuming prime-to-p degree everywhere
p is arbitrary; in particular p = 2 is included, so the argument may not use the odd-prime even/odd idempotent splitting
rho is an even character of Delta_0 with rho not trivial; the trivial character is handled separately (Remark b))

the passage from X and E_infinity/C_infinity to their plus counterparts is justified by Greither's Remark a) only up to a power of p, because mu = 0 for E_infinity/C_infinity is not available at that point; he notes char(X_rho) is prime to p, which makes the replacement legitimate in the proof of Thm. 3.1
the proof accumulates factors p and (gamma - 1) which are removed at the end using mu = 0 (Ferrero-Washington) and Leopoldt's conjecture
proofSteps: Greither states that the proof is 'a very technical matter; the principal ideas are already contained in the relevant papers of Kolyvagin and Rubin', i.e. an Euler-system/Kolyvagin-derivative argument adapted to the abelian, all-p setting.

The proof begins with Lemma 3.5, quoted as Rubin Lemma 2.3: for K/Q real abelian, M a power of p, and a prime ell congruent to 1 mod M splitting totally in K, there is a unique G-equivariant map with prescribed properties. That lemma was read only in its opening statement.
The removal of the accumulated factors p and (gamma - 1) at the end uses mu = 0 and Leopoldt's conjecture, both treated by Greither as available inputs.
acceptance: Check that the mu = 0 input is the Ferrero-Washington theorem, supplied independently, and is NOT derived from the main conjecture being proved.
Check the plus/minus replacement in Remark a): it is justified only up to a p-power factor, and Greither's justification uses that char(X_rho) is prime to p.
Check the trivial-character case separately (Remark b)), where both characteristic ideals are the unit ideal.
Check that the conclusion is a divisibility; equality is asserted only as a byproduct of the proof of Thm. 3.2 (Remark c)).

nodes.title: Greither's odd-character main conjecture with the one-half normalisation (Thm. 3.2)
nodes.statement: Let F/Q be abelian, unramified at p (p arbitrary, including p = 2), with the notation above. For every ODD character chi of Delta_0 not equal to omega, setting rho = omega chi^{-1}, one has char(X_chi) = ((1/2) G_p(T,rho)) as ideals of Lambda_chi = O_p(chi)[[T]] when rho is not trivial, and char(X_chi) = ((1/2) G_p(T,rho)(T - q_0)) = (1) when rho is trivial. Here G_p(T,psi) (psi even, viewed as a primitive p-adic Dirichlet character) is the element of Quot(Z_p(psi)[[T]]) written f(T,psi) in Washington p. 122, characterised by L_p(s,psi) = G_p(u^s - 1, psi) for s in Z_p (s not 1 for psi trivial), with u = 1 + q_0; for psi nontrivial (1/2) G_p(T,psi) lies in Z_p(psi)[[T]], and for psi trivial (1/2) G_p(T,psi)(T - q_0) lies in Z_p(psi)[[T]] and is a unit (Greither p. 452, citing Washington p. 125). The introduction's version of the theorem also records the canonical isomorphism (X/im X^+)_chi = X_chi for chi odd. The factor 1/2 is part of the normalisation, and the case chi = omega is genuinely excluded and handled by showing X_omega is finite.
hypotheses: F/Q abelian and unramified at p; p arbitrary, so p = 2 is included and the odd-prime plus/minus idempotent splitting is NOT assumed
chi is odd and chi is not omega; the excluded character omega is treated separately by proving X_omega finite (odd p via Mazur-Wiles p. 183; p = 2 by F = Q or Q(i) with X itself zero)
for rho trivial the power series G_p(T,rho) has a pole and must be multiplied by (T - q_0) to become a unit of Z_p(psi)[[T]]; this is the pole/augmentation correction
the one-half factor is present throughout and is the normalisation that makes the odd-character statement match the Stickelberger/B_{1,chi^{-1}} normalisation of Thms. A and B
the final equality (rather than divisibility) uses the analytic class number formula for minus class groups

Cor. 2.14 and Prop. 3.4 are statements after tensoring with Q_p (Greither remarks that Greenberg analysed the Kummer pairing for p = 2 without tensoring by Q_2); the integral ideal identities in the proof of 3.1 => 3.2 therefore rely on the absence of p-power discrepancies (mu = 0), which the pages read do not spell out
proofSteps: The implication Thm. 3.1 => Thm. 3.2 is 'a well-known argument (cf. Rubin p. 415-416, and Greenberg Sec. 2)' involving the direct limit A_infinity = lim A(K_n) and the Galois group Y of the maximal abelian p-ramified p-extension of K_infinity.
Lemma 3.3: X is quasi-isomorphic to Hom_{Z_p}(A_infinity, Q/Z) over Lambda', with the explicit CAUTION that Lambda' acts via a f(a) = f(sigma a) and not via the inverse map.
Prop. 3.4 (Kummer pairing, as in Greenberg, after tensoring with Q_p): V_rho(Y^+) = V_chi(X)^*(1), i.e. in odd notation V_chi(X) = V_rho(Y^+)^*(1), with chi = omega rho^{-1}.

Start from the two exact sequences 0 -> U_infinity/E_infinity -> Y -> X -> 0 (class field theory) and 0 -> E_infinity/C_infinity -> U_infinity/C_infinity -> U_infinity/E_infinity -> 0 (tautological). By Thm. 3.1, h_rho char(X) = char((E_infinity/C_infinity)_rho) for some h_rho; multiplicativity of char on short exact sequences then gives h_rho char(Y_rho) = char((U_infinity/C_infinity)_rho) = char((Lambda_chi/((1/2) G_p(T,rho)))^*(1)) by Cor. 2.14 (a statement over Q_p Lambda, see the L3 local-unit node).

By Prop. 3.4, char(Y_rho) = char(X_chi^*(1)); hence char(X_chi) divides char(Lambda_chi/((1/2) G_p(T,rho))) = ((1/2) G_p(T,rho)) for all odd chi not omega. Finiteness of X_omega gives char(X_omega) = (1), and the analytic class number formula for minus class groups upgrades the divisibility to equality.

Check the exclusion of chi = omega and the two separate arguments used for odd p and for p = 2.
Check that Lemma 3.3's Lambda'-action convention is the non-inverted one; using the inverse action changes the characteristic ideal by the involution.
Check the pole factor (T - q_0) for trivial rho and that it makes the ideal the unit ideal.

nodes.title: Greither's arithmetic consequences at p = 2 and the real counterpart
nodes.statement: Theorem A: if F/Q is abelian imaginary, unramified at 2, with Galois group Delta whose 2-Sylow subgroup Delta_2 is CYCLIC, then for every odd 2-adic character chi of Delta which is NOT of 2-power order, |A_2(F)_chi| is given by the stated power of |(1/2) B_{1,chi^{-1}}|_2, with exponent d(chi) = [O(chi) : Z_2] and the convention |a|_2 = 2^{-r} for a = 2^r u, u a unit of O(chi). Theorem B (= Thm. 4.1) is the divisibility for the quotient A_2(F)_chi / im A_2(F^+)_chi from which Greither derives Thm. A (he shows that B implies A, after remarking that it is enough to prove a divisibility in Thm. A). Theorem C: if F is real and Delta_p is cyclic, then for all characters chi of Delta whose order is not a power of p and which are FAITHFUL on Delta_p, |A'_p(F)_chi| is given by the corresponding power of |L_p(1,chi)|_p, where A'_p(F) is the p-part of the projective limit of the ray class groups Cl_{p^nu}(F). Greither notes that some condition on Delta_2 is necessary (examples show this) and that a corollary of Thm. A is a sharpening of Stickelberger's theorem at p = 2.
hypotheses: Theorem A requires F imaginary abelian UNRAMIFIED AT 2 and Delta_2 CYCLIC; Greither states explicitly that 'Examples show that some condition on Delta_2 is necessary'

the characters in Thm. A are odd and NOT of 2-power order; up to Q_2-conjugacy there is exactly one odd character of 2-power order, treated separately via the analytic class number formula in Remark b)
the normalisation on the right-hand side is (1/2) B_{1,chi^{-1}}, i.e. the same one-half factor as in Thm. 3.2
Theorem C requires chi faithful on Delta_p and of order not a power of p; A'_p(F) is INFINITE and only (1 - e_epsilon) A'_p(F) is finite
the deduction of Thm. A from Thm. B uses the analytic class number formula, the computation k_F = k_L of the kernel |ker(A_2(F) -> A_2(L))|, and Q_L = 1
proofSteps: Greither reduces Thm. A to Thm. B (a divisibility for the quotient by the image of the real part) and derives Thm. B from the main conjecture Thm. 3.2 in his Sec. 4.

The derivation of Thm. A from Thm. B compares the product over all odd chi with chi restricted to Delta_0 nontrivial (modulo Q_2-conjugacy) of the two sides, using the analytic class number formula and the identity |A_2(F)_chi| = |A_2(F)_chi / im A_2(F^+)_chi| valid because chi is odd and the norm A_2(F) -> A_2(F^+) is onto.
Sec. 4, where Thms. B and C are actually proved from the main conjecture, was NOT read for this packet.
acceptance: Check that the cyclicity hypothesis on Delta_2 is retained; Greither states a counterexample-based necessity for some such condition.
Check the one-half normalisation in Thm. A against the one in Thm. 3.2, and against any other source's Stickelberger normalisation, before comparing.
Check the Q_2-conjugacy bookkeeping and the exceptional odd character of 2-power order, handled by the analytic class number formula rather than by the main conjecture.
Check Thm. C's ray-class group A'_p(F): it is infinite, and only its (1 - e_epsilon)-part is finite, so the stated cardinality is for that part.
